fourier.help:
Fourier Samples: curate a sample library into device-ready folders for hardware samplers.

New here? `fourier demo` tries it on a generated library, and `fourier setup` sets it up
for yours. Each command's --help says more.

params.help: Show the version and exit.
params.name: version

params.help: Path to the library database (default: $FOURIER_HOME/library.duckdb, or an older home's library.db)
params.name: db

params.help: fourier.toml to use (default: $FOURIER_CONFIG, ./fourier.toml, ~/.config/fourier/fourier.toml; FOURIER_CONFIG=none for none)
params.name: config_path

params.help: Override one tunable for this run, over every config layer (repeatable)
params.name: sets

params.help: Debug logging, and the audio libraries' warnings (librosa, numba)
params.name: verbose

fourier build.help:
Build the master, one step after another: scan the library for new and changed files
(Sononym's analysis and Live's tags too, when they're there), analyze what's new, curate
the CATEGORY/family/file folders and verify them. A whole build (no CATEGORY, or --all)
replaces the master only when every category built and verify passed.

Curating clusters each category's CLAP embeddings into families, names each family from
what its sounds share, picks the samples that represent it best, and exports WAV. On a
terminal the Build and Verify stages show a summary and keep the rest in a log
(<home>/logs); --verbose prints it all.

 
  fourier build                     # everything (as --all); the first run analyzes the library
  fourier build -j 6                # the same, six categories at a time
  fourier build --dry-run           # files, disk space and time per category; writes nothing
  fourier build KICKS --out /tmp/k  # one category, into a scratch folder
  fourier build --all --no-scan     # from the database as it is (no scan, no analysis)

params.help: Output root (default: the master, $FOURIER_CURATED_DIR or [output] master)
params.name: out_dir

params.help: Samples per family folder
params.name: per_family

params.help: Min CLAP phrase z-score for a phrase to lead a folder name
params.name: clap_z

params.help: Copy aif/mp3 verbatim instead of converting to 16-bit WAV
params.name: no_transcode

params.help: Folder descriptions from a local LLM (Ollama); default: DESCRIBE, off
params.name: describe

params.help: Build every category (what `fourier build` does when no CATEGORY is given)
params.name: do_all

params.help: Rebuild the CLAP index from the DB first if it is stale
params.name: rebuild_index

params.help: Build ADDITIVELY as a superset of this published version (e.g. v2): copy it verbatim, add only new samples, never move/remove existing paths
params.name: base

params.help: Parallel category workers for --all (process pool; per-category output is identical to serial)
params.name: jobs

params.help: Skip the per-kind trim/loudness export pass (copy/transcode verbatim)
params.name: no_loudness

params.help: With --base: add only samples whose library path contains this (a new pack)
params.name: only_pack

params.help: With --base: add only samples scanned on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD)
params.name: since

params.help: With --base: share of each category's budget it may grow by (default 0.15)
params.name: allowance

params.help: --all: keep the categories an unfinished build already made, if nothing changed
params.name: resume

params.help: Print files and disk space per category (every category unless one is given), and what size = auto does; write nothing
params.name: dry_run

params.help: Skip the scan and the analysis: build from the database as it is
params.name: no_scan

params.help: Build even when a linked folder in the library is unavailable (its samples are left out)
params.name: allow_missing

params.help: Everything the Build and Verify stages say (default: on when the output isn't a terminal); --quiet: a summary, with the rest in a log file
params.name: verbose

fourier build.short_help: Scan and analyze what's new, build the master and verify it.

fourier config.help:
Your settings: what the config layers resolve to (preset, overlay, fourier.toml,
--set), what each setting does, and `config edit` to change them.

 
  fourier config edit              # open fourier.toml in your text editor
  fourier config show              # what's in effect, and where each value came from
  fourier config explain words     # what one setting does
fourier config.short_help: Show, explain or edit your settings (fourier.toml).

fourier config edit.help:
Open the fourier.toml in use in a text editor: $VISUAL or $EDITOR when set, else the
system's (TextEdit on a Mac). It's a plain text file of `name = value` lines; save it and
the next command uses it. `fourier config show` checks what it sets.
fourier config edit.short_help: Open your fourier.toml in a text editor.

fourier config explain.help:
One tunable: its class, the knob that sets it, its default and current value. A knob
(scale, size, tempo, ...): what it does and the tunables behind it. `categories`
instead: every folder the taxonomy makes, with example files.

params.help: For a setting: the exact rule and the advanced settings behind it
params.name: detail

fourier config explain.short_help: Explain one setting, or list the category folders.

fourier config show.help:
The preset, the knobs the config files set, and each tunable that differs from the
code's default with the layer that set it (--all: every tunable).

params.help: Every tunable, not just the overridden ones
params.name: show_all

fourier config show.short_help: Show the preset, knobs and tunables the config sets.

fourier demo.help:
A first run that can't touch anything of yours: generate a small synthetic library,
analyze it with stand-in data, build the master and render it for the Digitakt 2 and the
M8, all inside one folder with its own Fourier home and config. Needs no samples, no
model and no download; takes a minute or two.

 
  fourier demo
  fourier demo --dir /tmp/fourier-demo

params.help: The sandbox folder: new, empty, or an earlier demo's (default: ./fourier-demo)
params.name: root

fourier demo.short_help: Try Fourier Samples on a generated library, in a sandbox folder.

fourier devices.help:
The device profiles: what each device plays and its limits, each value cited from the
device's manual or marked a convention or unverified. The package's are in
config/devices; your own go in ~/.config/fourier/devices (or the folders in
$FOURIER_DEVICES), where `fourier devices new` writes them. Your device isn't listed?
Make a profile with `fourier devices new`.

 
  fourier devices list
  fourier devices show m8_tracker
  fourier devices new
fourier devices.short_help: List, show and make device profiles.

fourier devices list.help:
List the device profiles: format, how samples are loaded, storage, and whether the
values are checked against the manual.

fourier devices new.help:
Make a device profile of your own: asks what the device plays and how its files are
organized (each answer can be given as an option instead), writes it with every value
`status: unverified` to ~/.config/fourier/devices/<id>.yaml, and loads it to check it.
The comment at its top says how to cite the manual (docs/device-profiles.md, on GitHub:
https://github.com/bvk7787/fourier-samples/blob/main/docs/device-profiles.md).

 
  fourier devices new
  fourier devices new --name "My Sampler" --load card --card-dir /Samples \
      --sample-rate 48000 --bit-depth 16 --max-path 255 --yes

params.help: The device's name, e.g. "My Sampler"
params.name: name

params.help: The profile's id (default: from the name, e.g. my_sampler)
params.name: device_id

params.help: How samples get on: card: the device reads an SD card or USB drive (fourier sync copies the render onto it); transfer: its maker's app sends files and never overwrites one; folder: you copy the render yourself (a DAW, a computer folder)
params.name: load_way

params.help: The rate the device plays
params.name: sample_rate

params.help: Bit depth (8 only if the device takes it)
params.name: bit_depth

params.help: stereo: keep each file's channels; mono: fold every file to one
params.name: channels

params.help: File format the device reads
params.name: fmt

params.help: The folder on the card the render goes in (a card device), e.g. /Samples
params.name: card_dir

params.help: 2: CATEGORY/family folders; 1: CATEGORY folders, the family in the file name
params.name: folder_depth

params.help: Most files in one folder (0: no limit)
params.name: files_per_folder

params.help: Longest file path the device takes, card folder included (0: no limit)
params.name: max_path

params.help: Longest file or folder name (0: no limit)
params.name: max_name

params.help: Longest file in seconds (0: no limit)
params.name: max_seconds

params.help: Storage for samples in GB (0: don't say)
params.name: storage_gb

params.help: Plain-ASCII file and folder names (accents dropped), for devices that show only ASCII
params.name: ascii_names

params.help: Folder to write it to (default: ~/.config/fourier/devices, or the first of $FOURIER_DEVICES)
params.name: out_dir

params.help: Ask nothing: the default for every value not given
params.name: yes

params.help: Replace a profile of your own with the same id
params.name: force

fourier devices new.short_help: Make a profile for a device that isn't listed.

fourier devices show.help:
Show a device profile: each value with the manual page it comes from, or its status
(convention, unverified).
fourier devices show.short_help: Show a device profile, each value with its source.

fourier diff.help:
What changed between two builds: folders renamed / new / gone, files added,
removed or moved. OLD and NEW are master folders, manifest files or archived build
stamps (~/.fourier/builds); defaults: the previous archived build vs your current master.

 
  fourier diff
  fourier diff ~/Music/FourierCurated.prev ~/Music/FourierCurated
fourier diff.short_help: Show what changed between two builds.

fourier doctor.help:
Check what a build needs: the config, the library and its database (and how many of
its files a cloud drive keeps only online), the providers (Sononym, Live, the built-in
fallback), the analysis, the CLAP model and index, and the devices, and estimate the
analysis and build time (from this machine's last runs, else built-in reference rates).
OK is ready, WARN worth a look, NEXT what the first build does itself (scan, analyze, index,
download the model) and FAIL what would stop a build; it exits non-zero only on a FAIL.

 
  fourier doctor
fourier doctor.short_help: Check what a build needs and estimate how long it takes.

fourier open.help:
Show one of Fourier's folders in your file browser (Finder on a Mac): the master
(the default), the renders (one device's with DEVICE), the releases, the build logs, the
Fourier home, or `config`: your fourier.toml in a text editor (as `fourier config edit`).
`report` writes a page about the master and opens it in your web browser: every
category and family with a play button for each file, where it came from, what the last
build left out and why, and Keep / Drop / Misfiled buttons that export a CSV for
`fourier review import`.

 
  fourier open                      # the master
  fourier open report               # listen, understand and rate in your web browser
  fourier open renders digitakt_2   # the folder to drag into Elektron Transfer
  fourier open logs                 # every build's full log

params.help: Print the path instead of opening it
params.name: print_only

fourier open.short_help: Show the master, its report page, a render or the logs.

fourier publish.help:
Cut an immutable release from the master (releases/v<N> under the publish root).

Your working draft is the master ([output] master, ~/Music/FourierCurated by default):
rebuild and iterate there freely; nothing touches the releases until you publish.
Publishing copies the master to <publish root>/releases/v<N>, immutable and recorded in
the database, for transfer to hardware. It never overwrites a release unless --force,
and never one a device lock uses.

 
  fourier publish --dry-run          # what the release would change, against the last one
  fourier publish --notes "first set"

params.help: Master dir (default: $FOURIER_CURATED_DIR or ~/Music/FourierCurated)
params.name: src

params.help: Publish root (default: [output] publish, else ~/Music/Fourier)
params.name: root

params.help: Release notes
params.name: notes

params.help: Force this release version number
params.name: as_version

params.help: Overwrite an existing release version
params.name: force

params.help: (deprecated; publish always cuts a release now)
params.name: as_release

params.help: Preview what the release would change against the last one (or --base); copy nothing. Exits non-zero when it would move, change or remove a released file
params.name: dry_run

params.help: With --dry-run: the release to compare with (default: the latest)
params.name: base

params.help: Publish even if `fourier verify` fails (a release is permanent: avoid)
params.name: no_verify

fourier publish.short_help: Cut an immutable release from the master.

fourier releases.help:
The releases on disk and which is LATEST, and any problem with the releases folder
(subcommands: the database's record of them).

 
  fourier releases
  fourier releases recorded
  fourier releases import v1     # record a release the database doesn't know

params.help: Publish root (default: [output] publish, else ~/Music/Fourier)
params.name: root

fourier releases.short_help: List the releases on disk and which is LATEST.

fourier releases import.help:
Record a published release (v1, v2, ...) in the database's release tables, for one
published before the database knew it (publish records it).
fourier releases import.short_help: Record a published release in the database.

fourier releases recorded.help: List the releases the database records.
fourier releases recorded.short_help: List the releases the database records.

fourier render.help:
Render the master (or a release) for a device: its sample rate, bit depth, channels,
folder depth and path limits. Paths already on the device (its path lock, written when
you render a release) never change: locked files keep their names and original audio,
and retired ones stay in the image.

 
  fourier render m8_tracker                   # preview from the master
  fourier render m8_tracker --release v1      # render v1 for transfer; locks paths
  fourier render m8_tracker --dry-run         # what it would change on the device
  fourier render m8_tracker --check           # on-card paths vs the path-length limit
  fourier render digitakt_2 --release v2 --new-only   # and v2's new files on their own

params.help: Master dir to render from (default: the master)
params.name: master_dir

params.help: Render an immutable release (e.g. v1) instead of the master, and lock its paths
params.name: release

params.help: With --release: render without recording new paths in the device lock
params.name: no_lock

params.help: Output dir (default: [output] renders, else FourierRenders beside the master)
params.name: out_dir

params.help: Cap the rendered image size in MB (default: full)
params.name: max_mb

params.help: Only check the on-card paths against the device's path-length limit
params.name: check

params.help: With --check: the folder the render is copied to (default: paths.card_dir)
params.name: card_dir

params.help: Only preview what the render would change on the device (its path lock); exits non-zero when a path on the device would lose its audio
params.name: dry_run

params.help: With --release: also put the files this release adds to the device in a folder of their own (<render>-new-in-vN), to copy across on their own
params.name: new_only

fourier render.short_help: Render the master or a release for a device.

fourier review.help:
The listening loop: rate the master's files Keep, Drop or Misfiled, and the next build
follows the ratings (a Keep stays, a Drop goes, a Misfiled moves). Rate with `review
rate` or `review import` (a CSV file), or in Ableton Live's browser with tags
(Fourier|Keep / Drop / Misfiled / Move-<CAT>) that `review ratings` harvests. All of
them write the same ratings store ($FOURIER_HOME/ratings.json).

 
Without Live: rate, import, queue, score, misfiles.
Needs Live:   ratings (it harvests Live's tags; queue, score and builds harvest them
              too when Live has tagged the master).

 
  fourier review rate "Kick 01" keep
  fourier review rate "Snare Tight 03" misfiled --to CLAPS
  fourier review import ratings.csv   # columns: path (or name), rating, category
  fourier review queue                # the next files to listen to, in <master>/_REVIEW
  fourier review score                # a build against the ratings
  fourier review misfiles --dry-run
fourier review.short_help: The listening loop: rate files, import ratings, queue and score.

fourier review import.help:
Import ratings from a CSV file with a header row: `path` (or `name`: anything `review
rate` takes), `rating` (keep, drop or misfiled) and an optional `category` (for
misfiled: the category it belongs in). Rows that match no file, or several, are listed
and skipped (exit 1); the rest are stored as `review rate` stores them.

 
  path,rating,category
  KICKS/punchy/Kick_01.wav,keep,
  Snare Tight 03,misfiled,CLAPS

params.help: Master the files are in (default: your master)
params.name: master_dir

params.help: Match the rows and report, store nothing
params.name: dry_run

fourier review import.short_help: Import ratings from a CSV file, without Live.

fourier review misfiles.help:
Treat the misfile detector's most confident calls as Misfiled (next build re-homes them).

Stored apart from your ratings; any rating you give a file wins.

params.help: Min margin (other-folder minus own-folder similarity); default 0.4
params.name: margin

params.help: Master (default: your master)
params.name: master_dir

params.help: List detections, store nothing
params.name: dry_run

params.help: Remove all automatic detections
params.name: clear

fourier review misfiles.short_help: Mark the misfile detector's confident calls.

fourier review queue.help:
Build a review queue in <master>/_REVIEW: the samples whose rating teaches Fourier Samples most.

Saves the previous queue's tags first (harvest + write-back into the master), then
picks suspected misfiles, shaky placements, neighbors of your Drops, and random spot
checks. Tag them in Live like anything else, or rate them with `review rate` (a queue
file's name works as its QUERY).

params.help: Files in the queue
params.name: n

params.help: Master (default: your master)
params.name: master_dir

fourier review queue.short_help: Queue the files whose rating teaches the most.

fourier review rate.help:
Rate one of the master's files: keep (it stays), drop (the next build leaves it out) or
misfiled (the next build moves it to another category; --to names which); clear removes
a rating given here or imported (also one whose file is gone from the master or the
library). QUERY is what `fourier why` takes: a source path, a master path
(KICKS/family/file.wav) or a piece of a file name or library path. When it matches
several files, you pick one.

 
  fourier review rate "Kick 01" keep
  fourier review rate KICKS/punchy/Kick_01.wav drop
  fourier review rate "Snare Tight 03" misfiled --to CLAPS
  fourier review rate "Kick 01" clear

params.help: With misfiled: the category it belongs in (the next build puts it there)
params.name: move_to

params.help: Master the file is in (default: your master)
params.name: master_dir

fourier review rate.short_help: Rate one file Keep, Drop or Misfiled, without Live.

fourier review ratings.help:
Harvest Fourier|Keep / Drop / Misfiled tags (Ableton browser) into the ratings store.
Needs Ableton Live: without it, rate with `review rate` or `review import`.

A Favorite (red Collection) on an untagged file counts as Keep; --apply then writes
the Keep tag into Live right away.

params.help: Master to harvest (default: your master)
params.name: master_dir

params.help: Also write stored ratings back into the master as Live tags
params.name: do_apply

fourier review ratings.short_help: Harvest the rating tags from Live's browser (needs Live).

fourier review score.help:
Score a built master against your ratings (harvests Live's tags from your master
first, when it has any).

params.help: Built master to score (default: your master); e.g. a temp build before swapping it in
params.name: master_dir

fourier review score.short_help: Score a build against the ratings.

fourier search.help:
Search the library: by words that describe the sound, by a reference file, or by
filters.

QUERY (or --like TEXT) and --like-file compare sounds with CLAP: they need the CLAP
model and index (`fourier setup` installs the model; `fourier build` makes the index).
--class, --categories and the
brightness, noisiness, harmonicity and peak filters read Sononym's analysis and use its
vocabulary, so they apply only when the library was scanned from Sononym; duration, BPM
and favorites work without it.

 
Examples:
  fourier search dark sub-heavy kick --top 20
  fourier search --like-file ~/Desktop/reference.wav --top 20
  fourier search --min-dur 1.0 --max-dur 4.0 --bpm-min 160 --bpm-max 180
With Sononym:
  fourier search --class Loop --bpm-min 160 --bpm-max 180 --bpm-octave
  fourier search --categories "XFX Sweeps & Lasers,XFX Whooshes & Whips" --min-dur 1.0
  fourier search metal hit --categories "Perc Metal Hits"

params.help: Sononym's class (OneShot or Loop)
params.name: cls

params.help: Comma-separated Sononym category names (e.g. 'XFX Sweeps & Lasers,Tone Pads & Textures')
params.name: categories

params.help: Min duration in seconds
params.name: min_dur

params.help: Max duration in seconds
params.name: max_dur

params.help: Sononym's brightness, 0 to 1
params.name: brightness_min

params.help: Sononym's noisiness, 0 to 1
params.name: noisiness_min

params.help: Sononym's harmonicity, 0 to 1
params.name: harmonicity_min

params.help: Min BPM: a loop's tempo as a build resolves it (one-shots never match)
params.name: bpm_min

params.help: Max BPM
params.name: bpm_max

params.help: Also match loops at half or double the tempo
params.name: bpm_octave

params.help: Sononym's min peak dB (e.g. -12)
params.name: peak_min

params.help: Only samples marked as favorites
params.name: favorites_only

params.help: How many results to show
params.name: top

params.help: Text describing the sound (CLAP), the same as QUERY. E.g. 'dark sub kick'
params.name: like_text

params.help: An audio file to find similar sounds to (CLAP)
params.name: like_file

fourier search.short_help: Search the library by sound (CLAP) or by filters.

fourier setup.help:
Set Fourier Samples up for your library, step by step: where your samples are, your
devices and style, the config file, the CLAP model a build needs, an optional local LLM,
and a check of everything. Each step says what it's for and can be skipped; run it
again any time.

 
  fourier setup
  fourier setup --yes --library ~/Samples --device digitakt_2 --preset balanced
  fourier setup --yes --force --library ~/Samples --device m8_tracker   # replace a config

params.help: A folder of samples (repeatable, or comma-separated)
params.name: library

params.help: A device id (repeatable, or comma-separated; fourier devices list)
params.name: devices

params.help: The style: balanced (the default), breaks-acid, hiphop-lofi, house-techno, ambient-cinematic, trap, or a preset file
params.name: preset

params.help: Where the master goes (default: ~/Music/FourierCurated; FourierCurated-<config name> for a config --to puts elsewhere)
params.name: master

params.help: Where device renders go (default: beside the master)
params.name: renders

params.help: Where releases go (default: ~/Music/Fourier; Fourier-<config name> for a config --to puts elsewhere)
params.name: publish

params.help: Where to write the config (default: ~/.config/fourier/fourier.toml); another path is a second library's, with its own master, renders and releases
params.name: path

params.help: Replace an existing config
params.name: force

params.help: Install the CLAP model a build needs (default: ask; yes with --yes); when it's installed, update PyTorch and Transformers (default: ask; no with --yes)
params.name: clap

params.help: Set up folder descriptions with a local LLM (default: ask; no with --yes)
params.name: llm

params.help: Without Sononym, let a build train a sound model on your library's own names (default: on; --no-sound-model writes SOUND_TRAIN = false to the config)
params.name: sound_model

params.help: How big a set: starter (about 1 GB), standard (about 3 GB), full (the style's own size; the default), or a card size like 4GB
params.name: size

params.help: prepared: melodic one-shots tuned to C, loops levelled, tidy names (the default); as-is: every sound as it is, with its own name
params.name: processing

params.help: Start `fourier build` at the end (default: ask; no with --yes)
params.name: build

params.help: Ask nothing: the options given, defaults for the rest
params.name: yes

fourier setup.short_help: Set Fourier Samples up for your library, step by step.

fourier sync.help:
Copy a device render onto a mounted card, such as the M8's SD card.

VOLUME must be where the card is mounted (/Volumes/M8, /media/<you>/M8), or a card an
earlier sync wrote to; --force takes any other folder. Copies into <VOLUME><card_dir>
(M8: /Samples/Fourier) with rsync (or Python) and without
extended attributes, so macOS writes no "._" AppleDouble twins onto the FAT/exFAT card
(they show up in the device's browser as .wav files that fail to load). Dotfiles
(the render marker, .DS_Store) are skipped, any "._" file under the target is removed,
and the audio file count on the card is checked against the render.

 
  fourier sync m8_tracker /Volumes/M8

params.help: Render to copy (default: [output] renders, else FourierRenders beside the master, /<device_id>)
params.name: render_dir

params.help: Also remove files in the card folder (<card_dir>) that the render doesn't have (refused if it holds a file neither this render nor an earlier sync made)
params.name: delete

params.help: Show what would be copied
params.name: dry_run

params.help: Sync into VOLUME even when it isn't a mounted card or drive (a folder you chose)
params.name: force

fourier sync.short_help: Copy a device render onto a mounted SD card.

fourier tools.help:
Power tools for the steps `fourier build` runs for you, and for looking after the
library and its database.

 
  fourier tools scan               # bring new and changed files into the database
  fourier tools analyze --status   # how far each analysis step has got
  fourier tools train              # train the sound model on your library
  fourier tools audit              # what the master leaves out of the library
  fourier tools import-folder ~/Downloads/new-pack
fourier tools.short_help: Power tools: scan, analyze, audit, imports and the database.

fourier tools analyze.help:
Analyze the audio curation reads, step by step (`fourier build` does this after its
scan). Incremental: only samples not done yet. The steps: derived features (from
Sononym's), librosa features, CLAP embeddings and their index, sample-chain events,
quality, Sononym's folded tempo, loop trims, Fourier's own roots (pYIN) and keys, and the
sound model's labels (without Sononym, trained on the library first when it has none).
Fourier's own analysis runs with or without Sononym; `--only own` fills it in on a
library analyzed before it existed.
Files a cloud drive keeps only online are skipped unless --download is given.

 
  fourier tools analyze
  fourier tools analyze --only clap
  fourier tools analyze --only own
  fourier tools analyze --status

params.help: Just this step (repeatable)
params.name: only

fourier tools audit.help:
Audit the master against the whole library for blind spots: kinds of sound the
library has plenty of and the master barely covers.

Three lenses: the classifier's categories the master leaves uncovered, CLAP
nearest-neighbor coverage (regions far from every pick, clustered and named by a local
LLM when Ollama runs), and packs big in the library but thin in the master.

 
  fourier tools audit
  fourier tools audit --out ~/audit.md

params.help: Master to audit (default: $FOURIER_CURATED_DIR)
params.name: master_dir

params.help: Write the markdown report to this path
params.name: out_path

params.help: Nearest-curated-cosine threshold below which a sample counts as poorly covered
params.name: far

fourier tools audit.short_help: Find what the master leaves out of the library.

fourier tools db-stats.help:
Show what the library database holds: samples, favorites, and with Sononym's data its
categories (count, average length, brightness and noisiness; the names `fourier search
--categories` takes). --missing lists samples whose files are gone (--prune removes
them); --metadata checks the classifiers' labels against their sources;
--disagreements lists where Sononym's readings and Fourier's own differ, a place to look
for misfiled samples.

 
  fourier tools db-stats
  fourier tools db-stats --missing --prune
  fourier tools db-stats --metadata --shadow
  fourier tools db-stats --disagreements --examples 30

params.help: Also list samples whose files are no longer on disk
params.name: missing

params.help: With --missing: remove those samples from the database
params.name: prune

params.help: Also check each provider's labels and descriptors against its source (exits 1 on any difference)
params.name: metadata

params.help: With --metadata: rebuild every provider's labels and descriptors first
params.name: do_rebuild

params.help: With --metadata: also score the path and audio providers against Sononym
params.name: shadow

params.help: Also list samples where Sononym and Fourier's own analysis disagree (one-shot or loop, tempo beyond an octave, pitched, root note, and the sound model's category): a report, nothing changes
params.name: disagreements

params.help: With --metadata or --disagreements: differences to print (of each kind)
params.name: examples

fourier tools db-stats.short_help: Show what the database holds; check files and metadata.

fourier tools dedup.help:
Find samples that share the same content hash (the first 8 KB of the file): the same
file in more than one pack or folder. Nothing on disk changes.

 
In each group, the one kept is chosen by:
  1. a favorite first
  2. the highest sample rate
  3. the longest
  4. the earliest scanned

With --hide, the other copies are marked hidden in the database, so `fourier search`
leaves them out; builds don't use the mark.

 
  fourier tools dedup --dry-run
  fourier tools dedup --hide

params.help: Mark redundant copies as hidden (is_hidden=True)
params.name: hide

params.help: Report duplicates without making changes
params.name: dry_run

fourier tools dedup.short_help: Find copies of the same file in the library.

fourier tools import-folder.help:
Copy a folder of audio into a library folder (with several library folders, pass
--to). The only command that writes into the library, and it only adds copies.

Copies WAV/AIFF/FLAC verbatim and decodes OGG/Opus/MP3/CAF to WAV. A file whose extension an
enabled preparer names (a codec soundfile lacks) is written as WAV. The source folder
is never modified. Re-runnable: incremental by default, --clean wipes and reloads.

 
  fourier tools import-folder ~/Downloads/new-pack

params.help: Destination (default: <library>/<the source folder's name>)
params.name: dest_root

params.help: Copy .ogg as-is instead of decoding it to WAV
params.name: no_convert_ogg

params.help: Don't offer files to the preparers fourier.toml enables (fourier/preparers.py)
params.name: no_preparers

params.help: Skip source files larger than N MB (0 = no cap).
params.name: max_mb

params.help: Wipe the destination first (default: incremental, skip unchanged)
params.name: clean

params.help: Use an existing destination that holds only earlier imports (marks it as one)
params.name: adopt

fourier tools import-folder.short_help: Copy a folder of audio into a library folder.

fourier tools resolve.help:
Store each sample's resolution between the two classifiers (Sononym and Live's tags)
in the sample_resolution table: its home category, how well they agree, and both
classifiers' labels, so the second opinion can be queried across the library.

 
  fourier tools resolve
fourier tools resolve.short_help: Store each sample's resolved category for queries.

fourier tools scan.help:
Bring the library into the database (`fourier build` does this first): Sononym's
analysis when it's there (new and changed samples), otherwise a walk of the library
folders (fourier.toml's library), then Live's auto-tags when Live's file index is there.

The walk reads every audio file soundfile can (.wav .aif .aiff .aifc .flac .mp3 .ogg
.opus .caf), follows folder symlinks that lead out of the library folder, says what it
skipped, and marks samples it no longer finds missing (a build leaves them out). A
library folder that is missing or empty (an unmounted drive) stops it, and nothing is
marked. With Sononym, --walk walks too: the files it adds wait for Sononym's analysis
before a build uses them, and samples whose files are gone are left out of builds.

 
  fourier tools scan
  fourier tools scan --only files
  fourier tools scan --walk          # Sononym, then a walk of the library folders
  fourier tools scan --prune

params.help: Just this source (repeatable)
params.name: only

params.help: Sononym: also drop samples Sononym no longer has
params.name: prune

params.help: With Sononym: also walk the library folders (adds the files it hasn't indexed, marks samples whose files are gone)
params.name: walk

fourier tools scan.short_help: Bring new and changed library files into the database.

fourier tools train.help:
Train the sound model on your library: a small classifier over each sample's CLAP
embedding and Fourier's own measurements, taught by how your sample makers named their
files and folders (and your ratings), never by Sononym's or Live's analysis. About a
minute; it reads the database only. Without Sononym a build trains one by itself once
your library's names label enough samples, and places with it what no name rule
recognizes; this trains it now (or again). A model is kept only when it's reliable on the
packs it didn't learn from (--keep keeps it anyway). The weights and the report stay in
your Fourier home: they're learned from your library, whose licences are yours.

 
  fourier tools train
  fourier tools analyze --only sound    # label the library with it (a build does this)

params.help: Where the weights go (default: <Fourier home>/sound_model.npz, where builds look)
params.name: out

params.help: Where the training report goes (default: beside the weights)
params.name: report

params.help: Pull the weights toward the taxonomy's CLAP prompts instead of zero
params.name: clap_prior

params.help: Keep the model even when it isn't reliable on the packs it didn't learn from
params.name: keep

fourier tools train.short_help: Train the sound model on your library (it stays on this machine).

fourier verify.help:
Check the master against every curation rule (it runs after each build and before
publish), and with --render in scratch device renders: manifest against disk, budgets,
names, ratings, routing, sample chains, length caps, identical audio, DC and more. Exits
non-zero on any FAIL.

 
  fourier verify
  fourier verify --render m8_tracker --render digitakt_2
  fourier verify --quick

params.help: Master to verify (default: your master)
params.name: master_dir

params.help: Also render for this device into a scratch dir and check it (repeatable)
params.name: renders

params.help: Keep the scratch renders in this dir
params.name: keep

params.help: Skip the checks that read every file's audio
params.name: no_audio

params.help: Skip DB-backed checks (sample chains, twins, hygiene)
params.name: no_db

params.help: Only the quick invariants (budgets, ceilings, vendor cap, hygiene, names)
params.name: quick

fourier verify.short_help: Check the master against every curation rule.

fourier why.help:
Where a sample landed and which routing rule put it there, or, for one the master left
out, why the last build left it out (the per-vendor share, a near-duplicate of which
file, a category's gate, the budget, or a category the library can't fill). QUERY is a
full source path or a piece of a file name / library path.

 
  fourier why "Kick Round 03"
  fourier why --rules
  fourier why --unrecognized

params.help: Master to look in (default: your master).
params.name: master_dir

params.help: Print the routing precedence table and exit.
params.name: rules

params.help: Most samples to explain (default 5), or to list with --unrecognized (default 20).
params.name: limit

params.help: List the samples no name rule recognized, and those recognized that no category took (without Sononym), and what to do about them.
params.name: unrecognized

params.help: Every rule that matched, the classifiers' votes and labels, and the scores
params.name: detail

fourier why.short_help: Show where a sample landed and which rule put it there.
